title: Trump presidential library foundation: settlement money, Miami land, IRS status
summary: Documented: the first Trump Presidential Library Fund (incorporated Dec 2024) was administratively dissolved in Sept 2025. A successor Donald J. Trump Presidential Library Foundation (May 2025; trustees Eric Trump, Michael Boulos and James Kiley) won IRS exemption in 10 days during the Oct 2025 shutdown and was deeded the Miami Dade College parcel (county-assessed at $67M+) for $10, with two lawsuits failing so far to stop it. The weakest element is '$60M+ unaccounted for': Trump's June 2026 disclosure shows $56.5M paid to the foundation and $8M from X paid to Trump personally, so lawmakers now allege $6.5M-$14.5M missing plus $7M unexplained. The 747 transfer to the foundation is the stated plan, but it is not settled.

sub_claims.statement: The first library fund was dissolved in Sept 2025 and ~$60M+ of settlement money earmarked for the library is unaccounted for, per Warren, Blumenthal and Stansbury.
sub_claims.finding: The fund was incorporated in Florida on 20 Dec 2024 by Trump-entity lawyer Jacob Roth and administratively dissolved in late Sept 2025 for not filing an annual report. The lawmakers' March-April 2026 letters alleged up to $63M lacked any public accounting. Trump's OGE disclosure, released 30 Jun 2026, then showed $64.5M in total: $56.5M paid to the Foundation by Meta, ABC and Paramount, and $8M paid by X to Trump personally. The lawmakers' 16 Jul 2026 letter alleges $6.5M-$14.5M missing and $7M of unexplained spending against the Foundation's reported $50M of revenue (as of 10 Oct 2025). The dissolution and the allegation are documented, but 'unaccounted for' now refers to a much smaller gap, and that gap remains an allegation.

sub_claims.statement: A successor foundation received Miami Dade College land worth $67M+ for $10.
sub_claims.finding: The MDC trustees voted on 23 Sep 2025 to give the ~2.6-acre downtown parcel to the state. DeSantis and the Cabinet (Board of Trustees of the Internal Improvement Trust Fund) voted unanimously on 30 Sep 2025 to deed it to the foundation for $10, on condition that construction starts within five years. The county appraiser's 2025 assessment is more than $67M; one report cites a $60M appraisal, and plaintiffs estimate ~$300M market value. The deed was recorded in Jan-Feb 2026.

sub_claims.statement: The foundation got fast-track IRS approval during the government shutdown.
sub_claims.finding: It applied on 10 Oct 2025 and received an IRS determination letter dated 20 Oct 2025, during the shutdown. Normal processing is 3-6 months, and lawyers called it 'virtually unheard of'. The request cited settlement money in limbo. The application projected ~$950M of contributions ($50M in 2025, $300M in 2026, $600M in 2027). The day after the approval, the IRS announced it would not process exemption applications for the rest of the shutdown (Miami Herald). The IRS declined comment, citing privacy. No evidence of political intervention was found; 'special treatment' is the Miami Herald's characterization.

sub_claims.statement: The Qatari 747 is slated to go to the library foundation.
sub_claims.finding: Per C16, the jet is to transfer to the foundation by 1 Jan 2029, and Bondi and White House counsel called this legally permissible. It flew as Air Force One from mid-2026. A White House official said there was 'no final decision'. In Oct 2026 Eric Trump told NBC that displaying it in Miami is 'not the plan at the moment' and that an older retired Air Force One would be shown instead.

sub_claims.statement: Foundation officers include Eric Trump, Michael Boulos and James Kiley.
sub_claims.finding: The May 2025 Florida incorporation lists Eric Trump (president and trustee), Michael Boulos (Tiffany Trump's husband) and James Kiley (an attorney who has represented Trump) as trustees. Tiffany Trump's inclusion is reported inconsistently and is unverified. The NYT found that a proposed budget allotted $400,000 to officers, while a Florida charity filing said none expected pay. The first fund's directors were not identified.

sub_claims.statement: The land transfer has been challenged in court.
sub_claims.finding: In the state case, Marvin Dunn's Sunshine Law suit won a pause and then a temporary injunction (Oct-Nov 2025, Judge Mavel Ruiz; Dunn posted his home as bond). It was dismissed on 18 Dec 2025 after the MDC board re-voted. In the federal case, Sistrunk Seeds (Dunn's Overtown Farm) et al. v. Trump et al. (S.D. Fla. 1:2026cv23365) was filed on 13 May 2026 by the Constitutional Accountability Center and Gelber Schachter & Greenberg under the Domestic Emoluments Clause, alleging the 'library' is a hotel venture. In Sept 2026 Judge Rodolfo Ruiz II stayed discovery and said the immunity and standing defenses could 'dispose of the entire case'. No final ruling was found as of Nov 2026.

sub_claims.statement: The foundation, White House and payers have explained the money trail.
sub_claims.finding: No on-record foundation response to reporters or to the lawmakers was found. The White House refers questions to the library. The companies told lawmakers they paid as their agreements required, without saying where the money went after the fund dissolved. The IRS declined comment.

corrections: Brief says ~$60M+ is unaccounted for; after Trump's 30 Jun 2026 disclosure, $56.5M is shown as paid to the foundation, and the lawmakers' current allegation is $6.5M-$14.5M missing plus $7M of unexplained expenditures.
X's settlement (~$8M per the disclosure, not the ~$10M press figure) was paid to Trump personally, not to the library.
$67M is the county assessed value; reported estimates range from a $60M appraisal to ~$300M market value.
The 747 transfer to the library is the stated plan, not settled; Eric Trump says it is not planned for display in Miami.
denials_and_context: The foundation has not responded publicly; the White House refers questions to it; the IRS cites privacy law.
Presidential library foundations are private nonprofits not required to disclose donors; no evidence that funds went to Trump family members has been shown, although the lawmakers ask.
The land transfer passed two public MDC votes and a unanimous Cabinet vote, and survived the state lawsuit; DeSantis and the CFO championed it.
The federal emoluments suit faces presidential-immunity and standing defenses that the judge signaled could end it.
The money allegations come from Democratic lawmakers; the underlying records (Sunbiz, IRS letter, OGE disclosure) are official.

leads.title: Library tower as a Trump hotel developed by the Trump Organization
leads.why_connected: Trump said the Miami library will 'most likely' be a hotel; Eric Trump (a foundation trustee) says the Trump Organization is developing it, which bears on whether the $10 public land gift benefits the family business.

leads.title: X's ~$8M settlement paid to Trump personally rather than the library
leads.why_connected: Trump's 2025 OGE disclosure lists the X payment as income to Trump, contrary to the assumption that all four settlements went to the library.

leads.title: Foundation officer pay discrepancy ($400K budget vs. no compensation filing)
leads.why_connected: Reporting on the foundation's Florida charity filing found a proposed budget allotting $400K to officers (Eric Trump, Boulos and two lawyers) while another filing said none would be paid (NYT finding relayed in search results; not independently fetched).

changes: Fresh searches (Warren/Stansbury releases and the July letter PDF, CPA Practice Advisor/WLRN reprints of the Miami Herald, CAC case page, Justia docket, Law&Crime, WLRN, Law360) confirmed every checked assertion. No final ruling in the federal case was found; Judge Ruiz signalled he may dismiss on immunity grounds, and CAC filed its opposition to the motions to dismiss on 15 Sep 2026. No Foundation response to the lawmakers was found.

Added a detail that strengthens the 'special treatment' context: the IRS announced the day after approval that it would stop processing exemption applications during the shutdown. Still no evidence of political intervention. Updated .md.
